# Warehouse operational fixture binding

This test-owned wrapper implements `umir-operational-fixtures/1.1.0`. It consumes the reviewed operational binding digest `de9c7bfc573ad0887be0f00b1ddc2495939469f58f3524c6dbb66a521fed385e`. C2 business contracts remain unchanged. Factory must use the complete reviewed dirty inventory with the retained Git HEAD and source identity; no public revision or selected pin is changed.

Build with Go 1.26.9 and GOWORK=off:

```sh
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /tmp/warehouse-fixture-server ./tests/fixtures/server
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o /tmp/warehouse-fixture-control ./tests/fixtures/control
docker build -f tests/fixtures/Dockerfile -t umir-local-warehouse-fixture .
```

The image runs UID/GID 65532, `/fixture-server serve`, and reads only `/run/umir-fixtures/config/config.json`. Its healthcheck is `/fixture-server healthcheck`. OwnerConfig must target warehouse, use private port 8080, public port 0, empty stateFile and null bootstrap. URLs name only the declared project services. Credentials are regular bounded 0600 files owned by the process, with no symlink ancestors or FIFO reads. Every key is distinct lowercase hex64. The service map contains exactly auth-warehouse, gateway-warehouse and serving-warehouse. The separate control reference is fixture-warehouse. Config identity hashes canonical nonsecret options and references. Binary identity hashes the running executable.

The wrapper uses public NewRegistry, NewScopedHTTPHandler, NewJWTVerifier and NewAuthSigningKeys. The real Auth JWKS URL is formed from the validated Auth base URL plus `/internal/auth/v1/jwks`; the actual private service key is used. No signer or identity bypass is supplied. Real registry runtimes own EventStore, SnapshotStore, event admission, projections and order attempts. The snapshot worker has cancellation and a completion path. Warehouse starts no expiry timer. Fresh processes create separate fresh instance and epoch UUIDs, empty business state and config-supplied clock checkpoint. Auth must reconcile the new epoch through its real lifecycle API. Unit tests use local peer doubles only; they do not establish J1/E acceptance.

The business listener contains no control route. Controls use POST `/fixture/v1/control` over a 0600 Unix socket in a 0700 owner directory. Invoke `/fixture-control request` with one request on stdin. The helper reads its own credential file, validates redacted replies and prints no provider error or credential. Controls support fixture.ready, clock.read, clock.set, clock.checkpoint, owner.fault.arm, owner.fault.read and owner.fault.clear. Jobs, bootstrap, scheduler and sink operations are unsupported. Readiness observes the real authenticated runtime and validated Auth discovery; absent Auth fails closed. A clock is healthy only because the same controlled function is wired into registry/admission/analytics, JWT checks and discovery cache validity. Host monotonic timers bound IO, fault duration and one-second failed JWKS retry throttling. The separate retry clock never determines JWT or key-cache validity. Transient discovery failure recovers at an unchanged owner instant. Owner-time cache expiry still refreshes immediately; stale keys fail closed.

Clock set compares instance/generation, rejects backward time and increments once, including equal instants. A canonical request replay returns its original result. Changed payload conflicts. At most 256 request IDs are retained with no eviction, eight controls run concurrently, requests are bounded to 16 KiB and depth 16, and IO is bounded to ten seconds. Checkpoint hashes canonical redacted clock JSON. The runner checkpoints and replaces private config before restart. No host-time reconstruction or automatic business-state reseeding is supplied.

Faults are one-shot decorators over real runtime methods. They match one operation and original command ID, expire after at most 30 seconds, and preserve passive command lookup and exact retries. Mutation operation IDs are registerProduct, defineDish, receiveDelivery, confirmWriteoff and commitOrder. Before-commit refuses before invoking the real mutation. After-real-commit-return-unknown requires a real recorded command and loses only the returned outcome. After-durable-before-reply requires that same observed commit and closes the actual response connection; Warehouse persistence remains in memory. Neither point claims a disk journal. A normal rejection or unresolved order is not promoted to committed.

The post-prepare point supports inventory and analyticsstock. Its synthetic commandID is the request JWT jti. The test response adapter reads that metadata only for correlation; the unchanged handler validates signature, claims, caller, role, scope and epoch before resolving the runtime. No new business header, endpoint, token, query or command-context file is added. Real PrepareStock commits pending facts before CalculateStock is faulted. Invalidation headers and retained pending quantities survive calculation failure. AnalyticsFault and the wrapper share one manager; the replaced separate mechanism was removed. Unsupported operation/point pairs fail closed.

Run `make check`, `make quality-test`, `go mod verify`, `go mod tidy -diff`, and `go test -race -count=1 -v ./tests/fixtures/...`. Build native and Linux amd64/arm64 binaries and the local test image. The import policy permits fixture-to-fixture composition, retains all production-to-test bans and denies fixture imports of peer services/Factory. Quality tests cover both directions. Independent W6 review, real Auth/Serving/Gateway bindings, real J1 assembly and E scenarios remain separate.
